featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

As expected from such an old and iconic restaurant, the place carries a beautiful old-world charm. The crowd was immense, and we had to wait nearly 30–45 minutes for a table. Seating is shared with other guests, which adds to the authentic traditional dining experience.

What truly stood out was the remarkably quick and efficient service despite the rush. We ordered dosa and filter coffee — the dosa was absolutely delicious, especially with the generous layer of fresh white butter that elevated the taste beautifully. The filter coffee was equally excellent and perfectly satisfying.

The restaurant is quite pocket-friendly, and the staff deserves appreciation for being extremely prompt, supportive, and well-managed amidst the heavy crowd. The only downside is the waiting time and constant rush; otherwise, everything about the experience was wonderful.

featured_reviews.name: Neel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Madras is one of the most iconic South Indian restaurants in Mumbai and truly lives up to its reputation. Located in the heart of Matunga, this place is famous for serving authentic and delicious South Indian food with consistent quality for decades. The moment you enter, the aroma of fresh filter coffee, ghee, and spices creates a warm and nostalgic feeling.
I tried their famous dosa and idli, and both were excellent. The dosa was perfectly crispy with a flavorful potato filling, while the idli was soft, fresh, and served with tasty chutneys and sambhar. Their filter coffee was another highlight — strong, aromatic, and refreshing. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient, which is impressive.
The restaurant maintains cleanliness and has a simple yet traditional atmosphere that adds to the experience. Prices are also reasonable considering the quality and popularity of the food. Overall, Cafe Madras is a must-visit place for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. It perfectly combines taste, tradition, and quality, making every visit memorable.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Primarily, a delivery outlet Charcoal eats serve awesome quick bites to munch on as late as 3 am during weekends and till 11 pm during weekdays. The place has seating arrangements too which I assume that hardly anybody show up for dine in whereas like most of us opt for delivery service from the outlet. It offers amazing biryanis and quick bites as the brand says it all - 'bite that good' and yes we do bite it good from Charcoal Eats. The delivery is outstanding with organised colourful packaging. I happened to go on for trying out their famous biryani and some quick bites right at their outlet in Dadar east. I found the interiors very attractive and cosy. Since the place has famed itself more into delivery but otheriwse I think it is also a chill place to dine in with family and friends.
Talking about my yummilicious orders, I had-
1) Peach Ice Tea - They serve beautiful glass bottles of 'Brewhouse' Peach Ice Tea. Its cute as well as amazing drink to opt for with the meal aside.
2) Barbeque Loaded Fries- Crispy potato fried topped with bbq sauce and some spicy masala were tasting too good when eaten hot.
3) Chicken Mughlai Paratha- Chicken chunks and onion mixture loaded inside fried parathas tasted just like the rolls.
4) Chicken Tikka Biryani- Reasonable price for the awesome biryani. Small chicken chunks beneath the fine layered biryani can be good to go to try this one.
5) Salted Caramel Mousse- The salty and sweet taste of this chocolate mousse is divine. Although not their in house production, but still this one would be loved be loved by all the sweet lovers just like me.
I totally loved this vibrant place. And it serves awesome quick bites and biryanis and moreover at decent price that could be the relevant reason for quick hogging to opt for from the same.

featured_reviews.review_text:

This time I ordered vegetarian and vegan dishes like Dum Baked Jackfruit Biryani, Afghani Makhmali Vegetarian Biryani, Dum Baked Aloo and Corn Biyani, Smoked Paneer Makhani Rice bowl and Kathal Haleem. As always they are of high quality, right quantity and worth the price. It comes in sustainable packaging making it a guilt free takeout choice.
I have noticed that usually when I takeout from anywhere, Non vegetarian food tastes way better and I always take advantage of choosing it as I live in a vegetarian house. While the Non vegetarian menu is fantastic, the vegetarian and vegan dishes are equally good! Thats why for the first time ever, I was thrilled to just order the vegetarian and vegan variants and I had no FOMO!

*Makhmali afgani chicken tikka  biryani - Absolutely loved this, mild flavoured creamy biryani with juicy pieces of grilled chicken.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.name: ATS
featured_reviews.review_text:
An iconic South Indian cuisine restaurant in the iconic Matunga east neighbourhood of Mumbai. Everything, I repeat, every damn food item here is par excellence.

Things eaten: Paniyaram, Rassam, Medu Vada, Kanchipuram idli, appam with coconut stew, mysore onion dosa, cheese pav bhaji, pineapple sheera AND filter coffee.

Verdict: The Medu vada is truly one of the best I have ever had. It is so soft yet crispy at the same time. The coconut chutney and Tamilian sambar is unparalleled. Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. Hygiene is as important as the taste and had they not compromised on the hygiene, my search for the 5-starred restaurant would have ended today. But alas the search continues!!

featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best south indian places to have breakfast/ lunch in Matunga. The ambience is pleasant and so is food. Menu is wide and many options are available for breakfast. South Indian thali is available for lunch. But overall I think the place is bit pricey.

featured_reviews.name: Shivesh Bhatt
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let's start with the 40 minute wait. When you're made to wait that long, you naturally expect something rewarding at the end of it...The ambience was good, and after waiting so long to get a table, we were genuinely happy to finally be seated. The place is moderately expensive, and honestly, nobody mind paying a premium if the experience justifies it. Unfortunately, the service here was pathetic

My friend asked for a bottle of water and specifically requested one at normal temperature. Even after more than 30 minutes, it didn't arrive. When it finally did, they brought chilled water instead. I understand weekends are busy and service may take longer than usual, but taking that much time for a simple bottle of water is ridiculous

Not wanting to waste any more time, we ordered Masala Papad. When it arrived, it had no sev on it. Upon asking, we were casually told that they didn't have available. At the prices you're charging, are customers supposed to simply accept a poorer experience without question?

Then came the next masterpiece. One of my friends ordered a Diet Coke. After waiting more than 10 minutes, the waiter brought a regular Coke. At that point, all of us started laughing because it had become almost comical. When we asked whether they even had Diet Coke, he confidently said they did. The problem was that he had already opened the regular can before asking to change it.

Unfortunately, the experience didn't stop there. We ordered Tandoori Rotis, and the first round arrived burnt to the point that they looked like coal. We told the waiter and politely requested that the next be made properly. The second round arrived looking exactly the same. When we pointed it out, the waiter simply replied, "Weekend hai sir, ho jata hai"

For God's sake, man, we're here to enjoy our weekend too. Why are you ruining the experience?

Throughout the evening, we kept laughing at all the things that kept going wrong because otherwise it would have been frustrating. But when the bill arrived, I genuinely felt compelled to write this review. I rarely leave negative reviews and have never written one this harsh before, but this experience left me with no choice :,)

featured_reviews.name: travofood
featured_reviews.review_text: A wholesome meal for 3 of us costed approx Rs. 1200.... And that too in this locality of Mumbai. the quality and the quantity also backs it up. The non veg portions are quite plentiful,so do consider this before ordering.parkingbis definitely a challenge in this area. So suggest u all to look for other alternatives while coming here.

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located at Colaba Causeway, this mughlai place is a pretty old and one of the legendary eateries which the city has to offer

The place has a royal ambiance but i believe they are definitely in a need of upgrade now.. especially the upper floors. The service is good.. initially it took a while for them to serve us as there was a huge corporate group having their party but once they had their attention to us.. they made sure that we are served well!

We went there for lunch, we ordered:
1) Roomali Roti: The roti was literally soft like a cushion and melts in your mouth, this is one of the best Roomali roti I have ever had.

2) Chicken Bhuna: Made on tawa, this boneless chicken bhuna was actually delicious. Chicken cooked was soft and melting in my mouth whereas the masala had right amount of spices to it and wasn't spicy which was to my liking!

3) Chicken Tikka Biryani: Usually the highlight of the restaurant, but to my surprise the biryani was better than what I had 1.5 years ago as it seems their chef has changed. The last time when I had it, the chicken was really dry and had been marinated in red color.. though it was charred well but was too dry! Whereas this time the tikka was properly marinated and grilled to the right amount leaving the chicken juicy and tender. The quantity served was good too. The rice i believe could have been more fluffier.

4) Sweet Fresh lime soda: The lemon concentrate at the bottom mixed with sugar and added soda.. mixed well.. definitely was refreshing but i wish they could add the fresh lemon juice for better taste.

Overall, a good place to have your fulfilling dinner.. the place had originally introduced to me by my mother.. though it might have changed over the time but still manages to have the same pull!

Hardeep Punjab - A Treat for Tandoori Lovers!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Visited Hardeep Punjab recently and was truly impressed by the flavors and the variety! We ordered the Non-Veg Platter, and it was a feast of smoky, juicy, and perfectly marinated delights. The platter included creamy chicken tikka, spicy seekh kebabs, prawns, and fish, each one cooked to perfection. The chutneys and pickled onions served alongside added that extra punch.

The menu offers a wide range of non-veg appetizers – from Chaska Maska Tikka to Thai Tikka – and everything sounded tempting. The place has a nostalgic charm with its classic Punjabi touch, established since 1988, and it's clear why it’s a favorite in the area.

Service was quick, portions were generous, and the taste was genuinely authentic. Whether you're with friends or family, this is a solid place to enjoy rich Punjabi flavors.

Must-try: Non-Veg Platter, Prawns Lasooni Tikka, and Chicken Lollipop
Will definitely be back to explore more from the menu!

Special Chai arrives in a huge glass, milky‑sweet with ginger bite, just enough to cut the fat. You break pav, drag it through keema, sip chai, repeat. featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Kasture
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bademiyan is one of Mumbai’s most iconic food spots, and it definitely lives up to its reputation. Located in Colaba, this place is especially famous for its late-night crowd and irresistible aroma of freshly grilled kebabs. The moment you arrive, you can see the energy—people waiting, food being prepared live, and the buzz of a true street food legend.

I tried the seekh kebabs, chicken tikka, and their signature rolls, and everything was cooked to perfection. The meat was juicy, well-marinated, and full of rich, smoky flavor. The rolls, in particular, are a must-have—perfectly wrapped, filling, and extremely satisfying. Portion sizes are decent, and the quality of ingredients stands out.

Service is quick despite the heavy rush, which is impressive. The staff is efficient and manages orders well, even during peak hours. Prices are slightly on the higher side compared to regular street vendors, but you’re paying for both taste and legacy.

Seating can be limited, and you might have to stand or wait, but that’s part of the authentic experience. Overall, Bademiyan is a must-visit for anyone who wants to enjoy classic Mumbai street-style Mughlai food.

Absolutely disgusting and deeply disappointing experience at Bade Miyan.

I ordered a chicken biryani and was horrified to find a cockroach in it while eating. Finding a cockroach in food is a serious hygiene and food safety issue, and it completely ruined the meal and the entire dining experience.

What was even more disappointing was how the situation was handled. We immediately brought the matter to the attention of the owner/management, expecting an apology, an explanation, and some accountability. Instead, the bill was quietly deleted/cancelled, and it appeared that the management was more interested in making the issue disappear than addressing the underlying hygiene problem.

This is not just about one spoiled meal. It is about customer safety, cleanliness, and how a business responds when a serious issue is reported. I have photographs of the cockroach in the biryani and am sharing them along with this review.

A restaurant’s reputation means nothing if basic hygiene standards are not maintained. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this place and would urge potential customers to consider this incident before deciding to dine here.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a restaurant 🏨 chain ⛓️ in Mumbai, known for its Mughlai 🍢 and non-veg food. I won't recommend this place much if you are Jain 👳or pure vegetarian 🥬. It's a 2 florey restaurant with AC 🌬️ and Non-AC 🪭 section usually the restaurant is packed during weekend. The name of the restaurant is BBC (Borivali Biryani 🍚 Center) known for its Biryani and majorly non-veg. If talking about the staff 🧑‍💼 they were occupied a lot and a bit ignorant about the customer 🙂, I asked 3-4 times for the same thing to different people still could not get much respond. The ambience ✨ of of Family restaurant and cleanliness 🧹 is maintained. Washroom is unisex and 🫧 clean however there was water blocked at some place.

Further, talking about the foods and the drinks that we tried :

1. Blue bliss - it's basically a lemonade 🍋 with an added food colour 🔵, it was sweet but an good option from the mocktail menu.

2. Virgin mojito 🍸- Just an old school taste of soda 🥤mixed with lemon 🧃 juice and with some basil 🌿 leafs in it.

3. Lemon Iced Tea ☕- It's a cool starter in drinks 🍷 to go with along with some heavy food.

3. Veg dum biryani 🌾- It's a simple option if you don't want to explore kuch and it's a safer option. I asked them to make it a bit spicy 🔥. A taste of mixed vegetables 🍆 and paneer served with boondi raita.

4. Paneer Crispy Plum  - It's a chinese sweet🍯 starter with some added veggies. I usually don't prefer sweets so I won't recommend the same.

5. Mushroom  🍄 Tikka - It's just like paneer tikka 🍢 but instead paneer mushroom 🍄 is used. For a change you can try mushrooms instead of Paneer.

The overall experience was okay as the staff was not attentive, the food taste in veg was not that good and I didn't have much to explore on the menu. You can go here for mughlai and kebabs dish 🍽️.
